blogs.title: From LSTMs to xLSTMs: Why Reviving Classic RNNs Matters for Modern AI
blogs.description: A lay‑person overview of the historical rise of LSTM networks, their decline with the advent of Transformers, and how the new xLSTM design blends old ideas with fresh innovations to close the performance gap.

blogs.title: Exponential Gating Explained: Giving Neural Networks a Second Chance to Forget
blogs.description: Dive into the concept of exponential gating, why traditional sigmoid gates limit a model’s ability to revise stored information, and how xLSTM’s new gating mechanism dramatically improves tasks like nearest‑neighbor search.

blogs.title: Memory Makeover: From Scalar Cells to Matrix Memories in xLSTM
blogs.description: Unpack the transition from a single scalar memory in classic LSTMs to the high‑capacity matrix memory of mLSTM, illustrating how this change boosts rare‑token prediction and associative recall.

blogs.title: Parallelizing Recurrent Networks: How mLSTM Breaks the Sequential Bottleneck
blogs.description: Explain how the mLSTM variant removes hidden‑to‑hidden dependencies, enabling GPU‑friendly parallel computation while retaining the benefits of recurrent memory.

blogs.title: Scaling LSTMs to Billions of Parameters: Lessons from Training xLSTM on 300 B Tokens
blogs.description: Summarize the large‑scale experiments that compare xLSTM with Transformers, SSMs, and other RNNs, focusing on perplexity results, context‑length extrapolation, and real‑world downstream task performance.

blogs.title: When Does Bigger Mean Better? Decoding the Scaling Laws of xLSTM vs. Transformers
blogs.description: Break down the power‑law scaling behavior observed for xLSTM models, showing why they keep a favorable performance offset as model size grows and what this means for future LLM development.

blogs.title: Practical Trade‑offs: Speed, Memory, and Parallelism in xLSTM Implementations
blogs.description: Discuss the engineering challenges behind xLSTM—CUDA kernel optimizations, matrix‑memory compute costs, and comparison of inference speed and throughput against popular Transformer and SSM models.
